title: How Video Editors Automate Repurposing Retainers With Claude #Shorts
description:
Video editors waste hours finding hooks in long podcasts. Learn how to use Claude Projects with timestamped transcripts to generate clip cut lists and B-roll cues. Note: Accurate timestamped captions are required; individual results vary.

1. Upload the full video transcript with timestamps into a Claude Project containing your editing templates
2. Prompt Claude to identify high-retention hooks and format a timed cut list with visual B-roll suggestions
3. Export the cut list straight into Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve to deliver fast repurposing packages

Tool used:
- name: Claude Projects
- endpoint: Extract 5 short clips with timestamps and B-roll cues from this transcript.
- docs: Claude Projects Knowledge Documentation

REPURPOSE_PROMPT.md (markdown) - Paste into your Claude Project chat with the transcript attached:
Analyze the attached timestamped transcript and extract the top 5 high-retention clips (30-60 seconds).
For each clip provide:
1. Exact start and end timestamps
2. Hook verbatim spoken dialogue
3. 3 specific B-roll visual ideas matching the pacing.

The catch: Claude reads text transcripts only; you must generate accurate timestamped captions before running the workflow.

Sources for the numbers:
- Agency editing case studies on transcript-based AI edit preparation workflows
- Anthropic Claude Projects documentation

Real ways to earn with AI, no hype - follow @GSXAutomation

This video uses an AI-generated presenter and voice.

clips.prompt: The man (my avatar) looks into the camera and talks to the viewer like a confident, friendly business tech explainer, smart and natural, not stiff; he turns from looking to the side to face the camera, leans in slightly and raises his eyebrows. Vertical 9:16 medium-wide shot from the knees up, camera about two metres away, his head in the upper third with space above it, both hands and all his gestures fully visible in the frame, static camera, sharp and well lit, wearing a navy unstructured blazer over a plain white t-shirt, in a professional video editing suite with two large monitors showing a colour-graded timeline, soft blue ambient light. His face, skin tone, hairstyle, beard, height and body build stay exactly as in my avatar's reference photos - the same natural average build, never slimmer and never heavier. He says, in clear natural English with a clear, neutral international accent, at a brisk, lively pace: "Video editors waste hours scrubbing podcast footage for short clips." His lips match every word. He starts speaking in the very first frame, with no pause before the first word, and stops right after the last word. Audio: only his voice - no music, no sound effects. No subtitles, no captions, no text on screen.
